title: Embedding window-slicing and kernel fingerprint profiling to reduce p99
creator: Sophia Cheng
description: Investigate and implement a runtime-level window-slicing strategy combined with lightweight kernel fingerprinting to pick optimized kernel paths and packet sizes for embedding requests. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency for the embeddings endpoint under mixed-size request traffic without regressing throughput or average latency. The work spans: (1) design of window-slicing (request packetization by token-count/tenant affinity), (2) micro-benchmarks to collect kernel fingerprints per model/sequence-length, (3) low-overhead fingerprinting probe in ingress to pick kernel hints, and (4) rollout plan with canary + telemetry to validate p99 reduction and throughput stability.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings endpoint reduced by >= 25% in staging for mixed traffic compared to baseline
no more than 5% throughput regression at 95th percentile load in our perf harness
runtime exposes a feature-flagged config for window-slicing and kernel-hinting
end-to-end observability: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, kernel-hint distribution, and fallback counts visible in Console
comments: 2025-02-19 — Spike completed: microbench harness shows that grouping small requests into 8-32k token windows reduces kernel setup overhead. Baseline p99 = 230ms, windowed p99 ≈ 170ms (local harness). — Sophia

2025-02-24 — Kernel fingerprint experiment: collecting ~2k samples across gpt-small and gpt-medium variants. Observed that int8 fused attention kernel outperforms generic matmul for short sequences but stalls for long kv-cache reuse patterns. We need a fingerprint that captures sequence-length distribution and kv-hit probability. — Marcus

2025-02-26 — Design decision: implement two-layer hinting. First, deterministic window slicing by tenant + token budget. Second, cheap fingerprint probe (first-token tokenization + last-kv tag) to pick between "fast-short" and "robust-long" kernel paths. Keep feature off by default. — Reviewed by Aisha Raman (SRE) and Diego Alvarez (Perf).

2025-02-28 — Perf run in staging (traffic replay using prod traces): p99 improved from 238ms -> 164ms, p95 unchanged, throughput -3% under sustained peak. Noted a small increase in CPU on the ingress host due to fingerprinting probes; added a mitigation to sample probes at 50% for high-throughput tenants. — Marcus

2025-03-01 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582 — implements window-slicer, kernel-hint API, and telemetry tags. Unit tests + integration harness included. Requesting review from infra and runtime teams. — Sophia
2025-03-02 — UX ask: Console needs new dashboard widgets showing kernel-hint distribution and per-route p99 deltas. Filed follow-up PM ticket PM-1248. — Marcus
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive windowing reduces kernel warmups but increases batching latency for isolated large requests; we mitigate with tenant-aware backoff and a hard cap on window delay (50ms). Kernel fingerprinting must remain low-cost — initial probe limited to first 2 tokens + kv-hit flag. If sampling overhead shows >8% CPU increase on ingress, we will revert sampling to 20% and prioritize server-side cache hints from routing layer.
next_steps: Complete code review and address infra feedback on PR #4582
Run 48-hour A/B in staging with production-sampled traces (rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Add Console panels and alert: embedding-kernel-hint-fallback-rate > 2%
Postmortem: if p99 improvement <20% in production, capture full trace logs for 1 hour and revert
